column1: # Hand-written English glosses for words whose Wiktionary glosses read badly
# out of context (mostly articles and pronouns). Everything else comes from
# lemma<TAB>gloss, or lemma<TAB>gloss<TAB>pos when the part of speech the
# pipeline would pick (that of the first Wiktionary entry with a usable
# gloss) isn't the one the gloss describes: "sino" is first a noun there.
# pos is one of: noun verb adj adv pron det article prep conj
# contraction num particle intj. A word with a pos other than verb gets no
# conjugation table. The build stops on a malformed row, a word listed twice,
# or a word that is also in exclude.txt.
# The commonest words where Wiktionary's first senses mislead: a rare or
# technical sense first, a misspelling's meaning, or a near-useless gloss.

column2: to take, to carry; to wear
to invite; to treat (to pay for)
to be quiet, to keep silent
